defect.evidence_quote: A finding of materiality of the evidence is required under Brady, supra, at 87. A new trial is required if “the false testimony could ... in any reasonable likelihood have affected the judgment of the jury . . . .”
defect.problem: The core holding is supported, but the frontmatter formulation is incomplete because it does not state the materiality/reasonable-likelihood limitation for relief. As framed, it can overstate nondisclosure of credibility evidence as automatically consequential.
defect.proposed_fix: Revise to: Impeachment evidence affecting a key witness's credibility, including an undisclosed promise of nonprosecution, falls within Brady/Napue; a new trial is required when the evidence is material, meaning it could in any reasonable likelihood have affected the jury's judgment.

reasons: The opinion supports the impeachment-evidence proposition: "When the “reliability of a given witness may well be determinative of guilt or innocence,” nondisclosure of evidence affecting credibility falls within this general rule."
The opinion also expressly requires materiality and applies that requirement to Taliento's testimony.
residual_risks: No separate inventory row tests the page's Rule quote or ^pin-154.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Add the materiality/reasonable-likelihood condition to the holding field.
